selection.reason: Baseline total segment length is 0.28 m while the frozen target [0.29, 0.035, 0.19] from a mount at z=0.15 sits roughly 0.295 m away and 0.04 m above the mount, so the arm must be nearly fully extended and must resist gravity droop. I therefore take both length parameters to their upper authorized bounds (near 0.16->0.17 m, far 0.12->0.13 m, total 0.30 m), raise the transverse section scale to its upper bound 1.05 which also increases the second moment of area and thus bending stiffness, and select the stiff material scenario (1.1x Young modulus, density and bending viscosity unchanged). Together these give a covered design (one length delta >= 0.001 m, section scale delta 0.05 >= 0.01, nonbaseline material) that is my engineering best guess for reaching this far, high target before spending any backend solve.
